title: Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: why baptism more useless on our view than theirs? — they also grant eternal damnation of reprobates, church-born baptism by command, and reprobation before birth
pass_a_gloss: This being premised, I ask why from our sentence Baptism administered about many infants is established as useless, and to seal nothing, rather than from the sentence of the adversaries. Is it because it is decreed unto God from all eternity to damn the reprobate? But this they themselves dare not deny. Is it because to be reprobated from the decree of God and to be baptized from the command of God are adverse unto each other? But they themselves also acknowledge that all born in the Church are to be baptized from the command of God, and that many of these nevertheless by the everlasting decree of God were reprobated before they were born. Or finally because they teach damnation fixed unto the everlasting, certain, and infallible knowledge of God, whereby as before his eyes he beheld a man bound with the guilt of sin? But we also profess the same.
pass_b_english: That premised, I ask why baptism of many infants is called useless and sealing nothing on our view rather than on theirs. Because God from all eternity decreed to damn the reprobate? They dare not deny that. Because reprobation by decree and baptism by command clash? They too grant that all born in the Church must be baptized by God's command, and that many of them were nonetheless reprobated by his eternal decree before they were born. Or because they teach damnation fixed in God's eternal, certain, infallible knowledge, whereby as before his eyes he saw a man bound by sin's guilt? We profess the same.
source_text: Hoc praemisso, quaero cur ex nostra sententia Baptismus circa multos infantes administratus inutilis statuatur, et nihil obsignare, potius quam ex sententia adversariorum. An quia Deo decretum est ab omni aeternitate damnare reprobatos? At hoc ipsi non audent negare. An quia Reprobari ex decreto Dei et Baptizari ex mandato Dei sibi adversentur? At ipsi etiam agnoscunt omnes in Ecclesia natos ex mandato Dei baptizandos, et multos horum nihilominus aeterno Dei decreto fuisse reprobatos antequam nascerentur. An denique quia illi damnationem infixam docent aeternae, certae et infallibili notitiae Dei, qua veluti ante oculos cernebat hominem peccati reatu constrictum? At nos etiam idem profitemur.
